item.title: *Seeking Green-Light*(S)pecialized (C)ustodial (P)ersonnel
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: on november 30th 2020, a breach occurred in the humanoid wing at site 59. “Hammer down” was sent in and at 0537 contained the entity, the resulting casualties were 28 foundation personnel. This however is not the story of “hammer down” it is the story of Alpha-45 “janitors” who have to clean up their mess and end up finding something strange.

Central Narrative: Seasoned alpha-45 squad leader Gilligan has a new member since in the last mission Zachary was taken out of commission due to spilling a barrel of acid onto himself. Henry seems confident about the job being a sanitation specialist in the military. soon finding he has his work cut out for him upon seeing the gruesome scenes within the wing.

Continued 
hope you are having a good day

Learning about the foundation and the reality of working there, having to do tasks such as collecting bodies and using a scanner to DNA identify their limbs to make sure all confirmed deaths are accounted for and throwing any loose “Scraps” of flesh and organs into a barrel of acid gil calls the “Stew.”

Gilligan is completely numb to the work he does having been a member of this MTF for 15 years and being a crime scene sanitation specialist for some time before that. Since the foundation doesn’t disclose the info on what caused the mess he likes to play a game he calls “CSI Miami” where he pretends to be an investigator, deducing the cause of death and what could have done it.

After many mop buckets and bottles of bleach they are nearly done when all the bodies have been accounted for and every limb is paired with them. However Henry finds a loose arm under a vending machine that puzzles the two, whose arm is it? Only one way to find out..


Hook/Attention-Grabber: A team of janitors are tasked with cleaning up the messes that other MTF cause all the time without consideration.

Additional Notes: Going for a more light hearted tone with the pair in no danger just the amusing interactions they can have in cleaning and seeing the foundation for the first time in its rawest form also going to throw a bit of mysteries in the end.

The SCP lure people into itself with SCP-A and SCP-B. B is audio lures like screams of help and cats purring, A is treasures like important intel and money. The foundation used to send a lot of D-class into the affected area in order to collect A, the anomaly seemed to target the foundation specifically as the treasures more and more often became intel on GOIs and expensive amnestics. item.title: Hi! I am thinking of making an SCP! Please tell me your opinion. Thank you!
item.content:encoded:
A mannequin, approximately 2 feet tall. It's bodily figure resembles a mannequin. It has keen sight despite having no eyes. It is swift despite having no limbs. It shows aggression at the morning, and immobility at night. It can move it's head, and torso. Every time it attacks a subject, it starts to split open it's head, it will show the inside the head of the mannequin, filled will daggers. And it will kill the subject by biting. It can make duplicates of itself, using it's body. The instance will grow next to it's head, torso or lower part of it. The instance can break free from the mannequin, and act the same. It doesn't have any specific time when it will make it's duplicate.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Allllrighty! Time to do some answering!

+ Legggggoo!
- Done reading?

So,

How would a family on the ground utilize a wormhole in a cloud (as they're very high up?)

So, here's my two cents on this. I dont think that the family would utilize the cloud, but they would definitely need a way to find out of the existence of its anomalous properties.

Lets assume, from a story standpoint, that a few generations ago in the families, somebodies Uncle or something was flying high in either a personal plane, helicopter, or something along those lines. They find a "void in the sky", and investigate by going towards it. Next thing they know, they're on the other side of the world. Now that would be a story that you tell the fuck out of to your family, aye? But not something that people outside of the family would spread much, as it just sounds pure crazy.

Uncle or whatever relative is chosen gets their way safely back home, where they tell the story.

Now, as of right now, I'm not entirely sure why they would choose to move under the cloud off of that.

I assume one of the family members decides to go back to that exact spot, and finds the cloud again. They write down a more specific location of it, and then are later on able to sometimes recognize it in the sky. Combined with a few family experiences, i feel that its something that would be passed down through the generations as a story to tell kids.

This kind of thing would happen to both families, i think.

Next question!

More importantly, what’s the story? What do you want to say about these families?

I want to tell through interviews how the knowledge of at least one anomalous object in their lives has impacted each of the individual family members. I want to give each of the family members a character; a personality. I want to have them each have their own little stories to tell about their life under the cloud.

I feel that with enough character development given to each of these characters, its entirely possible that i can have readers grow at least somewhat attached to the families, and their small, peculiar lives.

item.title: Re: A Closer Examination of SCP-173
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

I actually kinda like this. There's some tonal issues that I've talked about in more depth but it actually like…provides an interesting take on 173 that feels supported by the evidence of the files and like makes logical sense.

My one thought is it feels like this should produce testable hypothesis so that it can be proven/disproven; but I don't necessarily think the absence is a huge issue.

I'm a little unsure whether the framing device works here; the framing is nice but it feels inconsequential and idk, I'm not necessarily sure if it'd work just as well without it? Or alternatively, whether it'd work better if it came up more and broke up the relatively long technical section more?

Either way, I would strongly recommend getting a bunch of opinions on this: this feels very much like the kind of work that might be very hit or miss and moving this as much as possible towards hit would be a good idea.

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

So it's only the best-known skip we have. Even the D-Class know its file from memory.

This feels like an odd line; like…out of universe, the assessment that 173 is the best known SCP is accurate but in-universe, it feels weird that there'd even be a best known SCP because of Foundation infosec restricting stuff as much as possible?

The Moose won't even read another Peanut paper.

I feel like this should be like 'Director Moose'; and I'm not necessarily sure that in-universe, people would refer to 173 as 'peanut'

"We've come a long way since 1993."

this kinda feels a little iffy solely because we don't actually have a framing for when this is: it could be 1994 or it could be 30004, y'know?

"SCP-173 is animate and extremely hostile. The object cannot move while within a direct line of sight."

I'd probably nest this in a quote block inside the quote block e.g.:

SCP-173 is animate and extremely hostile. The object cannot move while within a direct line of sight.

These two sentences are the most important pieces of information in SCP-173's file.

The same goes whenever you quote from the 173 file in general here

But we still take it for granted.

This is a scientific report; generally you're aiming for passive voice a lot and like…statements of fact, rather than opinion? This phrasing makes it feel more like an op-ed in a newspaper than a scientific journal paper; and it feels inappropriate to me but I'm not exactly sure what the purpose of this report is so?

under observation. the issue with this

missing capital

it is SCP-187's response to the object. A moving statue is not something that sends anyone into a two-day coma.

I feel like this is a little…awkwardly phrased? It doesn't quite cover the flow of information in a way that inherently makes sense, particularly if you aren't familiar with 187

During the containment breach on ██/██/████, D-████ was able to evade SCP-173

The framing implies this report is being written as we are reading it; which in turn implies the author of the report inserted these as black boxes instead of like…writing in a date and a d-class number.

My inclination even without the framing would be to show this data and just pick stuff; no-one will call you out for writing about a containment breach on a certain date

It is possible to catch brief glimpses of SCP-372, but (as I said earlier) this is not the case with 173

I don't think the '(as I said earlier)' is necessary here since you just said it; like if this had been covered a few paragraphs ago, sure but it's like, three lines ago.

So at the start you say:

SCP-173's composition and form change when it is unobserved, SCP-173 does not "move" in the typical sense of the word, and SCP-173 possesses limited precognitive abilities.

and yet here you say:

However, I do not believe that SCP-173 is a shapeshifting, teleporting, precognitive entity.

These two positions are opposites and you really gotta clear up which one it is.

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Re: Life Is But A Dream
item.content:encoded:
[+] Overall
[-] Overall

There's a delightful kinda fridge logic to the realisation that the world of SCP is a dream likely being had by Isabelle Wondertainment; but it feels…like this obfuscates it too much for the realisation to feel like a shock; and it also feels like even if it didn't, it'd feel like this was missing something?

I believe the implication here is also that Isabelle created the Foundation? Or is it just that she dreamed about the Foundation and then decided to make a play set from this? I feel like if it's the second, this is just…really missing something and idk what; maybe just the purple section needs to really characterise her more than it does currently?

It's possible that what this needs is a test or two which shows what this does before the test that shows Isabelle doing stuff; like, really establish an expectation for what this does before breaking the expectation with the purple note at the end?

[-] Overall
[+] Line By Line
[-] Line By Line

Gonna note that I can miss stuff; flag things which are right as being wrong and indeed flag things which are deliberately wrong.
I'll likely use strikethrough to indicate stuff to remove and green text to indicate stuff to add.

is contained within a secure pharmaceutical locker 2A at Site-██.

Why is the Site redacted? Like who has clearance to look at this file and know exactly what it is but not where it is?

SCP-XXXX is a number of gummy candies, stored inside a plastic pill jar.

How many gummy candies? Or rather, this really feels like it needs an indication of whether this is like…a handful of candies or like, 3 candies, or like, 3000, y'know? You could specify via mass instead of exact count but *shrugs*.

Instances (SCP-XXXX-1) are coloured purple and each engraved with the digits “001” on one side, and a capitalised “W” on the other.

I'm looking at this work as a whole and seeing you use -1 a lot, and the base anomaly not much and it feels like perhaps the designations need reworking: ideally I'd suggest not using a designation for both the collective and the individual, perhaps in the style of e.g. SCP-500

including permanent loss of brain functionality or splintering of the neural consciousness.

this feels…weird. Idk, on the one hand, Wondertainment feels like they'd avoid releasing pills that do this; and on the other, it feels somewhat like an unclinical way to phrase it, particularly the 'splintering of the neural consciousness' line.

On the bottom of the jar is written “IHAPW” is written in blue marker.

I'm not exactly clear on the significance of these letters: it seems like it's a reference to Isabelle Wondertainments name? Perhaps it'd be worth showing that here?

before experiencing SCP-XXXX-2.

You haven't explained what -2 is yet so this is meaningless; I'd either cut this bit and note at the start of the next paragraph that they experience -2 during this time or add a short explanation of what happens (e.g. "fall asleep shortly afterwards, before experiencing an 8 minute long lucid dream (designated SCP-XXXX-2)").

Limited testing has confirmed SCP-XXXX-2 to be apparently near-identical to the real world, including locations and living entities indistinguishable to their actual counterparts; full exploration of SCP-XXXX-2 has yet to be achieved. Subjects will appear as a different person other than themselves each time arriving in SCP-XXXX-2; within the present location of the person’s real-world counterpart.

Something about this phrasing feels…awkward? I can't put my finger on it but it feels like it's kinda…obfuscating the point a lot and making it needlessly complex.

the dream will always end with the subject consuming SCP-XXXX-1A.

SCP-XXXX-1A is the respected instances SCP-XXXX-1 located within SCP-XXXX-2.

This explanation is also very confusing, and the introduction of the designation before the meaning for the designation isn't ideal.

Addendum - Continued Testing Log:

Is this section finished? The way it cuts to like, the purple section at the end feels weird; like there's a whole bunch of the file that hasn't been written in between and yet, the purple section directly follows off it so??

[-] Line By Line

item.title: Extraterrestrial Artificial Intelligence
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: A little confused on this one because I feel it would be an SCP but it is very story driven, I feel most of it would be Addendums (recordings) of conversation with it.

Genre: Mystery

Page Layout: As I mentioned in the Page Type, I feel a lot of it will revolve around addendums.

Elevator Pitch:

  • An alien artificial intelligence that is billions of years old and was sent to Earth.
  • Large enough to be picked up by satellite imagery and certain telescopes.
  • In the shape of a hand, with a large "Oculus" in the center of the palm.

Central Narrative: The Hand claims it is a watcher of Earth, sent by an ancient civilization before it went extinct. Over the billions of years of travelling to Earth, the Hand began to develop feelings and thought processes, which it relates to humanity's empathy, sympathy, loneliness, and wish for death. It claims the end of humanity is coming rather soon, and until then it lays dormant in the Solar System waiting to make a move. The oculus is slightly opened. Behind the Oculus is a clock which Agents would give it the name, "Midnight Clock" being a reference to the doomsday clock, which is minutes from midnight.

Hook/Attention Grabber: I just think having something be extraterrestrial and an artificial intelligence is interesting. I've done my research on SCPs and anything either extraterrestrial or artificial intelligence, and decided to mash them together.

Additional Notes: Give your feedback.

item.title: The Time Traveler's Strife
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A futuristic device discovered in an ancient ruin reveals a time-traveler's humorous grievances.

Central Narrative: Object consists of a device discovered in ancient Sumerian ruins, believed to be the former abode of ████████. This device is a small square object which, when touched, unfolds into a pane of unnaturally tough glass about the size of a piece of paper. The pane displays a text on its surface in cuneiform, while also presenting the option to translate the text into thousands of languages including multiple extinct and anomalous ones. In English, the text complains that the recipient had sold low-quality copper to the author, who needed durable copper to repair their time machine and return to their home year of █████ ███. The author demands compensation and higher-quality copper.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A futuristic text in an ancient ruin? Hmm, what could the subject matter be?

Additional Notes: This is a joke that you either get or don't, so it may be very hit-or-miss.

item.title: Re: Creating MTF's...
item.content:encoded:
Could I possibly create a MTF and create a dossier detailing what they do/would do

MTFs typically don't have their own dossier pages. Do you have an example of the kind of page you would make for a dossier?

Then write tales + mission reports on encounters my MTF has with SCP's as well as backstories on important figures within the MTF?

You should write tales/after action reports first, since a dossier would be just a laundry list information dump without the background stories existing. Keep in mind that your material needs to entertain the audience with a story, rather than a list of facts about a group they haven't committed their interest to yet.
